name: OCSP Response Parser
description: Parse an OCSP response to read the certificate status; the response signature is verified when trust roots are supplied.

examples.label: Verify a response with the test CA as trust root

hints.roots: Without trust roots the signature is **not** checked: the response is only read, not trusted.
hints.pair: The queried certificate and its issuer are required: the CertID in the response needs them to locate the target.
hints.status: The response status says whether the response itself succeeded; the certificate status is what tells you about revocation.

faq.a: The responder does not know this certificate, which usually means it is outside that responder's scope.

faq.q: Why does "verified" only appear with trust roots?
faq.a: The response is signed by the responder; checking it needs a certificate you trust.

faq.q: Can an OCSP request be parsed as a response?
faq.a: No, the encodings differ and DER parsing fails.
